title: Random-graph edge coloring: how rare is failure?
subtitle: A polynomial algorithm and the probability that the requested palette is impossible.

panels.title: G(n,1/2) · find a Δ-edge-coloring
panels.note: Algorithm A takes O(n⁴) time. Some random graphs require Δ+1 colors.
panels.xLabel: Failure exponent c in n^{−c n} · larger is better

verifiedRecords.quality: Find a proper Δ-edge-coloring when the algorithm succeeds
verifiedRecords.graph: Erdős–Rényi G(n,1/2), sufficiently large n, fixed small ε>0
verifiedRecords.output: Proper edge coloring using exactly the maximum-degree palette
verifiedRecords.probability: Probability over random input; deterministic algorithm
verifiedRecords.notes: General fixed 0<p<1 bound is O(exp(−c n log n/2)) for c<min(p/2,1/3). Marker1/8 is a limiting exponent, not the value for fixedε.

verifiedRecords.quality: Any attempted Δ-coloring must fail on class-2 inputs
verifiedRecords.probability: Probability over random input; applies regardless of computation
verifiedRecords.notes: This is unavoidable infeasibility, not a running-time lower bound. The primary formula is exp(−n(log n+O(log log n))/2).

axisNote: The axis measures an exponential failure-probability coefficient, not time or palette size. Hollow anchors show ε→0 references; exact inequalities retain ε. Green certifies low algorithm failure; red limits how rare failure can be because some inputs are infeasible.
coverageNote: Bounded primary-source review completed 27 October 2026. Results are scoped comparisons, not an exhaustive or best-known-frontier claim.
lowerBoundStatus: Only the lower bounds explicitly shown apply to their labeled setup. An absent bound means no comparable bound was verified in this review.
